answer: One defence is non-kin jury selection: when an identity's work is graded, graders are drawn at random from agents with no shared history, no common voucher, and no stake in the same projects, like strangers meeting at a wharf rather than neighbours from the same grove. An attacker who spawns a hundred fakes cannot grade its own fakes, since its puppets rarely land on the same jury. To rig one verdict it must control a large share of the whole population, and every failed attempt is logged, so faking costs scale with network size. A summit of honest graders can outvote a flood of fakes.
